items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 25 at 9:28AM PST until November 26 at 9:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Seas 10 to 15 ft.

* WHERE...Monterey Bay.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.

items.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 25 at 5:53AM PST until November 26 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Warning, significant coastal
flooding with up to 2.7 feet of inundation above ground level is
possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways.
For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of
20 to 30 feet.

* WHERE...Pacific Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 6 AM to 4 PM PST
Wednesday. For the High Surf Warning, through midnight PST
Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying
infrastructure, numerous road closures, and coastal erosion.
Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach
than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal
areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower
swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties,
and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and
increasing the risk of drowning.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...These predictions are approaching the
highest tide ever recorded. At the San Francisco tidal gauge,
high tide is expected to be 2.7 ft above normal (8.5 ft MLLW) at
10:49 AM Wednesday and 2.2 ft above normal (8.0 ft MLLW) at
11:38 AM Thursday. These predictions include up to 1.5 ft of
surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding
threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along
the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay,
respectively.
items.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. If
travel is required, do not drive around barricades or through
water of unknown depth.

Everyone should remain out of the water due to life-threatening
surf conditions. Stay off of jetties, piers, and other waterside
infrastructure.
